title: Mandala Rift concept paintings

hero.alt: A bell hangs over the riverside ghats facing a terraced pavilion, copper wheel, trading arcade and ember vessel at sunset.

description: Original, AI-generated environment and object paintings direct the materials, lighting and silhouettes in this fictional district. For built dimensions, use the registered plan and Blender views.

boards.title: Gates and gathering places
boards.alt: Four views of the southern trading gate, northern water gate, riverside bell terrace and indigo weighing court.
boards.prompt:
Produce original finished production concept paintings for YUGA, the Mandala Rift, a fictional 17th-century working Indian river city. Every image should resemble a carefully observed hand-painted environment or prop study for an ambitious PC game, with tactile weathered sandstone and ochre limewash, beaten copper with sparing verdigris, tarred dark teak, natural indigo, river jade, folded cloth and chisel marks. Clear tonal grouping. Late afternoon sun and sky bounce vary by panel. Reserve saturated highlights for story clues, keep walkable planes and door silhouettes legible. Compose without people, weapons, modern objects, writing, pseudo-script, logos, captions, watermarks, letters or ornamental page furniture. Use the specified camera and subject once per panel. Each panel fills its tile, with all important shapes inside its central 85%. Distinct local places in the SAME cohesive riverside district. Each scene is a finished painterly illustration with intentional shape language, material edges and atmospheric depth; avoid generic fantasy palaces or MMO loot splash art.

Deliver one landscape board with exactly four equal-size complete LANDSCAPE paintings in a precisely aligned 2-by-2 grid. Dividing lines at the exact horizontal and vertical midpoint, hairline separation at most; images may abut. No external margins, no asymmetrical panels, no titles. Do not allow any object, framing decoration, foreground or light to cross from one tile to another. Reading order is top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right.

TOP LEFT — Spice Gate. Street-level from the southern trade quay looking IN through a square post-and-beam arch. Deep red dried chillies on braided strings, yellow turmeric in low baskets, sacks, offset alcove and clear pale paving. Load-bearing lintels and old wheel ruts, morning light from the left. The wide walkable centre and interrupted side views say this is a team starting point.

TOP RIGHT — Water Gate. Look through a cool, broad northern water gate from under its shaded timber header towards an aqueduct stair. Three large upside-down terracotta water jars against a damp wall, worn copper spout, measuring grooves without lettering, a narrow teal channel and clear walking passage. Distinguish this sober hydraulic checkpoint from the spice gate.

BOTTOM LEFT — Ghat Mandapa. Human-eye view across a broad open river assembly terrace. An open sandstone pillared canopy, three ribbed bronze bell supports on its WESTERN edge, down-river glimpse through the colonnade and an empty circular flush copper intake in the ground. Quiet detail at head height, saffron rim and dovetailed stone piers. Monumental horizontal public pavilion, no pyramidal tower.

BOTTOM RIGHT — Bazaar Sanctuary. Look from a shaded indigo arcade into a compact DYERS AND WEIGHERS court, with a low weigh counter and square silhouetted scale gantry off to one side. A worn circular regulator fitting is flush in a warm open floor with sunlight falling across it. Suspended folds of indigo cloth and copper pans high at the edge, architectural detail subordinate to two clearly different exits.

Sand-rippled riverbed fully visible through the water, silt, stepping stones, reed rafts and clear pebbled landing on the opposite side. Spiralling brushstroke reflections and waterline lap marks, two contrasting banks still legible. Emphasize shallow wading, never a deep lake.

BOTTOM RIGHT — Reed Steps. Look diagonally DOWN a flight of broad worn sandstone steps into the river. Reed bundles are drying against the outside retaining wall, woven fish traps hang at the far side. Bright line on each nosing and hard shadow beneath, a dry side landing. A fan of golden reeds is its solitary distant recognition shape.

A large freestanding timber balance, open stone weigh-plinths and bronze standard weights arranged by diameter, flax ropes, carts and sacks entirely outside the central route. Stiff geometric shadows, warm ochre walls, a single cool awning. Show the public yard as a place where goods move.

BOTTOM RIGHT — South Temple. Eye level approaching a civic temple-side cloister of slightly battered sandstone columns and carved lotus brackets, with the ordinary walk continuing along the LEFT arcade. A second modest opening on the RIGHT has one large geometric V notch in its lintel. Beyond it reveal a surprisingly offset wall, a subtle optical impossibility, no glowing vortex, no script or idols.

TOP LEFT — South Pyramid. Player view FROM THE SHADOW just inside an arcade mouth looking OUT toward a stepped, four-tier southern sandstone pavilion over an open pass-through. This is the surrounding room under honey evening light, with oblique shadows and a dark indigo entrance awning.

TOP RIGHT — North Temple. A cool northern portico interior. Two parallel incised rectangular bars cut into a visible lintel announce its folded threshold. Through that door an interrupted corridor seems to turn left, while ordinary foot traffic would take a quiet column-and-limewash gallery to the right. River-reflected light falling upward onto a teak ceiling. Restrained, mysterious civic passage, open walking floor.

Two bars on the near entrance, an offset northern exit, a row of planted jars to one side; this side is pale grey gold and cooler, unlike the warm southern pavilion. No Egyptian spire, pyramid cap or desert.

BOTTOM RIGHT — Quarter-turn Pavilion. The architect’s standalone three-quarter axonometric exterior, a beautifully finished maquette against a neutral warm plaster field. Show the same original freestanding Indian sandstone pavilion on two rows of square piers, fully OPEN central through-passage, FOUR broad receding roof slabs (4 distinct horizontal eaves), low crown, roughly 10 m across and 9 m high. Plain return wall and single deep V notch over a threshold. Human-scale mortise pins and crisp carved mouldings. A whole building from base to roof, different from the player’s courtyard view.

Seen slightly from above with only a thin slice of river beyond and dry packed earth at its base; solid low silhouette.

TOP RIGHT — Sluice gearbox. A human-height square water-lift gearbox fixed on a stone plinth: riveted aged copper and blackened teak cover, one LARGE ratcheted cog half exposed, wound hemp rope, curved safety casing clearly cracked. Oblique close-up shows robust opaque silhouette, feet, physical joints and dry path beside it. Preindustrial mechanics, no steam pistons or electronics.

Show exactly THREE deep vertical worn bronze flanges: two modest side fins and a raised central rib whose bent tip points down toward a distant ring in the pavement. Narrow slivers of sun between the flanges, exceptional graphic readability against clear sky. An original civic machine detail, no text or writing.

BOTTOM RIGHT — Fold lintels. One comparative pair of monumental carved door-lintel fragments resting on piers in the same workshop, both in a single panel. One unmistakable incised CHEVRON V on the southern slab, exactly TWO deep parallel rectangular bar-grooves on the northern slab. Cool raking light inside the cuts and bare neutral stone everywhere else. No letters, scripts, mystic runes or flamboyant portal. Show how a mason could cut these symbols.

A long slender arm points to the right-hand open market exit. Side three-quarter view of the whole signal, believable ropes and pin, a distant soft limewashed street out of focus. Dominant elongated horizontal form. It is the stored water market’s recognition sign.

MIDDLE BAND — Ember vessel. Hero-object close three-quarter study on a single warm stone step, the entire squat hand-carried brass vessel fully visible: hammered round belly, two short real carrying handles either side, a pierced lid cradling a tiny living amber ember. Deep maroon linen strap and darkened soot below the perforations. A subtle point of warm light, carefully spaced utilitarian rivets. The vessel should be a unique recognizable game objective from several metres away.

BOTTOM BAND — Water ewer. Hero-object close three-quarter portrait of a distinct slender cool patinated-copper ewer with a long curved spout, flared narrow mouth and SINGLE elegant loop handle. A dark teal braided sling, matte ceramic foot, water beading around its lip. Complete profile and grounding shadow, blue sky reflected in rippled stone below. Its teardrop silhouette must be visibly unlike the squat ember pot, with no lettering or emblems.

room-atk.alt: A sunlit market street framed by a red sandstone gate, dried chilli strings, yellow roots and sacks.

room-b.title: Bazaar Sanctuary

room-mid.alt: A patched water wheel lifts copper cups above a stone bridge between an open river arch and the market.

room-bank.title: Dry Bank

room-ford.alt: Round stepping stones lead across shallow clear water toward reeds and a gravel landing.

room-steps_s.alt: Bundles of golden reeds and woven traps lean above low stone steps descending to the water.

room-temple_n.alt: Two horizontal grooves mark the pale portal opposite the ordinary timber-roofed colonnade.

route-atk-steps_s-walk.title: Spice Gate to Reed Steps · walk
route-atk-steps_s-walk.alt: Looking out of Spice Gate toward the Reed Steps, a bundled spice cart by the red gate gives way to a descending green canal street. Camera just behind the spice sacks, morning shadows, reeds appear at the far threshold.

route-atk-temple_s-walk.title: Spice Gate to South Temple · walk

route-atk-yard_s-walk.title: Spice Gate to Cloth Yard · walk
route-atk-yard_s-walk.alt: Spice Gate to Cloth Yard: dry long lane bent toward skeins of separated indigo and saffron cloth on bamboo lines; look back toward the orange ochre gateway from the approach, with a strip of sun as the path.

route-def-steps_n-walk.title: Water Gate to Jar Steps · walk

route-def-temple_n-walk.title: Water Gate to North Temple · walk

route-def-yard_n-walk.title: Water Gate to Scale Yard · walk

route-steps_s-ford-water.title: Reed Steps to Reed Ford · water
